get_concept.description: Read everything Thot publishes about one concept: its name in English, French and German (and any other language Thot has it in), the other names it goes by, where it sits among the broader and narrower terms, the XML value attached to it, the same concept in other vocabularies such as the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae, the works it is cited from, and (for a concept in the date thesaurus) the range it covers, both as Thot writes it and as numbers you can sort on. This is the one step behind a catalogue record that stores nothing but 'thot-374' and has to show a king's name and his dates.

get_thesaurus.description: Read a whole Thot thesaurus: every term in it, in the language you choose. The API serves a thesaurus as the nested source of a tree widget; this brings it back as rows, each carrying its identifier, the term above it, how deep it sits and the whole path down to it, so a workflow can filter and join it without walking a tree. A term Thot has not translated comes back in English and says so.

search_thesaurus.description: Find the concepts in a thesaurus whose term matches some text, closest match first. Every other step here needs a 'thot-' identifier and nothing in Thot turns a word into one, so this is where a workflow starts from a term someone typed. Case and accents are ignored, and each match comes back with the whole path down to it so a term that appears twice can be told apart.

description: Look up the Egyptological vocabulary published by Thot (Thesauri & Ontology for documenting Ancient Egyptian Resources), the University of Liège project whose seven thesauri give projects working on ancient Egyptian texts and monuments a shared set of terms for dates and reigns, languages, scripts, materials, techniques of inscription, text genres and the museums that hold them. Turn a 'thot-' identifier into a term in English, French or German, read a reign's date range as text and as numbers you can sort on, find the same concept in the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae, pull a whole thesaurus back as rows, search one for the term someone typed, or take a concept's SKOS record as RDF. No account or API key is required.
